nodes.summary: Large synthetic test suite for the return-report parser in sheets.ts covering Myntra, Ajio, Amazon, Meesho and Flipkart layouts, seller checks, identifier trust rules, repeat classification and product master parsing.

nodes.name: synth
nodes.summary: Builds a synthetic Myntra return row object with SYN- values, applying field overrides.

nodes.name: meeshoCsv
nodes.summary: Builds a synthetic Meesho CSV including the supplier preamble block, with options to omit or change the supplier.

nodes.name: meeshoRow
nodes.summary: Builds a synthetic Meesho return row with overridable AWB, link and SKU fields.

nodes.name: flipkartRow
nodes.summary: Builds a synthetic Flipkart return row matching the real Flipkart.csv headers, with overrides.

nodes.name: marketplace-rules.test.ts
nodes.summary: Synthetic tests for marketplace-rules: account ranking, header and return-type normalization, SKU variation handling, tracking link parsing, 15-digit AWB rounding resolution and courier partner detection.

nodes.name: oms-master-bridge.test.ts
nodes.summary: Synthetic tests for marketplaceForChannel, checking whole-word, case-insensitive channel-to-account mapping and null for ambiguous Myntra labels.

nodes.name: oms-orders.test.ts
nodes.summary: Synthetic tests for OMSGuru order helpers: order row normalization, personal-data redaction and usable lookup key extraction.

nodes.name: oms.test.ts
nodes.summary: Synthetic tests for the OMSGuru client and catalogue/SKU record builders: response envelopes, SKU/image normalization, throttle detection, credit-based waiting and request shapes with a fake fetch.

nodes.name: product-master-batch.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests for batched product master import helpers: 500-row batch limit, batch slicing and progress, staged import ownership/TTL checks and blank-image inheritance.

nodes.name: synRow
nodes.summary: Creates the n-th synthetic MasterRow with SYN- listing and product SKUs.

nodes.name: synEntry
nodes.summary: Builds a synthetic StagedMasterImport entry of generated rows with overridable owner and timestamps.

nodes.name: spreadsheet-numbers.test.ts

nodes.name: meeshoWorkbook
nodes.summary: Builds an in-memory Meesho XLSX workbook with a supplier block and one row holding the given AWB and tracking link.

nodes.name: unmapped-candidates.test.ts
nodes.summary: Synthetic tests for unmapped listing SKU resolution, checking article-suffix parents, spaceless variants, case-insensitivity and account scoping via listingSkuCandidates and unmappedIsResolved.

nodes.name: keysFor
nodes.summary: Builds the compact lookup key set for stored master entries the same way the resolver does.

nodes.name: upload-policy.test.ts
nodes.summary: Synthetic tests for upload activation rules: partial activation, fatal/no-access/empty-file blockers, pending rows, confirmations for untrusted identifiers or tracking disagreements, and duplicate counting.

nodes.name: row
nodes.summary: Creates a synthetic ParsedRow with valid defaults and field overrides for policy tests.

nodes.name: vms-catalog.test.ts
nodes.summary: Synthetic tests for the VMS catalogue integration: image/SKU cleaning, read-only SQL allowlist, TLS no-verify refusal, dedup rules, SQL chunk builders, fail-closed probe, category inference and SKU suffix stripping.

nodes.name: upload-policy.ts

nodes.name: countPreview
nodes.summary: Tallies a file's parsed rows into preview counts (scannable, pending, duplicate, untrusted identifier, cancelled, error and more).

nodes.name: stripNoiseSuffix
nodes.summary: Strips known seller, campaign and duplicate-size suffixes (e.g. _DIV, _KL, _YOU, _S_S, _New, _AI1) to yield the canonical master SKU.

nodes.name: cleanVmsImageUrl
nodes.summary: Keeps only http(s) image links and blanks anything else without repairing it.

nodes.name: cleanVmsSku
nodes.summary: Trims and length-caps a VMS SKU value.

nodes.name: cleanVmsCategory
nodes.summary: Trims and length-limits a category value, tolerating null.

nodes.name: inferCategoryFromTitle
nodes.summary: Infers an apparel category from a catalog title when the category column is blank.

nodes.name: normalizeVmsMarketplace
nodes.summary: Maps raw VMS channel names to canonical marketplaces (Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho, Myntra VB/EJ, Ajio, Shopify) or 'all'.

nodes.name: pickVmsColumn

nodes.name: dedupeVmsMappings

nodes.name: dedupeVmsRows

nodes.name: db.ts

nodes.name: isVmsConfigured

nodes.name: closeVmsPool

nodes.name: queryVmsReadOnly
nodes.summary: Runs a query on VMS only if it is a single SELECT/WITH without INTO, inside BEGIN READ ONLY with rollback on error.

nodes.name: fetchVmsCa

nodes.name: checkVmsConnection

nodes.name: follow-up-window.ts
nodes.summary: Engine-side gate for ticket follow-up cycles: reads the FOLLOWUP_NIGHTLY_ONLY opt-in (default is check-whenever-due), decides whether a cycle may lease a ticket given the shared 01:00-02:00 Asia/Kolkata window, and builds a window-status snapshot for the dashboard.

nodes.name: nightlyFollowUpOnly
nodes.summary: Parses the FOLLOWUP_NIGHTLY_ONLY environment variable, returning false when it is unset or one of 0/false/no/off (case-insensitive) and true otherwise.

nodes.name: shouldSkipFollowUpCycle
nodes.summary: Returns true when nightly-only mode is on and the given instant falls outside the nightly IST window, so the engine must not lease a follow-up ticket this cycle.

nodes.name: nightlyWindowStatus
nodes.summary: Builds a NightlyWindowStatus object (nightlyOnly flag, inWindow, next window start as ISO string, milliseconds until the window) for status display.

nodes.name: nightly-window.ts
nodes.summary: Pure, dependency-free time math for the Asia/Kolkata 01:00-02:00 claim-tracking window and the 48-hour post-submission eligibility rule; the Express server (reschedule path) and the desktop engine (lease gate) import this same file so the window cannot drift between them.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a fixed UTC+05:30 offset with Date UTC getters instead of Intl time-zone APIs; this is exact because IST has no daylight saving time.

nodes.name: istWallClock
nodes.summary: Converts a Date into Asia/Kolkata wall-clock fields (year, month, day, hour, minute) by shifting it by IST_OFFSET_MS and reading the UTC getters.

nodes.name: nightlyWindowStartForIstDay
nodes.summary: Returns the 01:00 IST instant on the IST calendar day that contains the given date.

nodes.name: isWithinNightlyWindow
nodes.summary: Checks whether an instant falls inside the half-open [01:00, 02:00) Asia/Kolkata nightly window.

nodes.name: isEligibleForNightlyCheck
nodes.summary: Rejects invalid dates and returns true only when the confirmed marketplace submission timestamp is at least FOLLOW_UP_ELIGIBILITY_HOURS (48h) older than now.

nodes.name: nextNightlyWindowStart
nodes.summary: Returns today's 01:00 IST window start if it has not passed yet, otherwise the next day's window start.

nodes.name: nextEligibleCheckAt
nodes.summary: Computes the next check time for an unresolved ticket: the 48h-cadence candidate, kept when it lands inside the nightly window and otherwise moved to the next window start.

nodes.name: msUntilNightlyWindow
nodes.summary: Returns 0 inside the nightly window, otherwise the non-negative milliseconds until the next window starts, for status display.

nodes.name: nightly-window.test.ts
nodes.summary: Pure node:test checks for the nightly tracking window, using fixed instants: window constants, IST wall-clock conversion, [01:00, 02:00) boundaries, 48h eligibility anchored on submission time, next-window calculation, and 48h candidate alignment.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README introduces the return-scanning app for VB Exports. Marketplace return reports from Myntra VB and EJ, Flipkart, Meesho, Amazon and Ajio are loaded as lookup data one account at a time, and every physical return is recorded in the return scan register, which is the permanent record. It also covers setup (npm run dev or RUN.bat), creating users from the CLI, the six web console pages, the Android scanner and the Windows desktop claim bot. AGENTS.md is the required starting point for contributors and lists the rules the rest of this tour shows in code: account scope on every data route, activation instead of replacement, and schema changes that only ever add.

tour.title: System Architecture Map
tour.description: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md is the map for the rest of the tour. One Express/PostgreSQL API serves three clients: the React 19 web console, the native Android scanner and the Electron desktop claim bot. The document traces the main data flows (sign-in, upload, scan, register, tickets, OMSGuru sync) and maps modules to files. package.json holds the pieces together as one ESM project, with scripts for the Vite + tsx dev loop, the esbuild server bundle and the Electron/NSIS desktop build, so keep this API-plus-three-clients picture in mind as the tour visits each part.

tour.title: Database Schema Foundation
tour.description: Everything rests on PostgreSQL. schema.sql defines the base tables: marketplaces, users and their account assignments, sessions, upload batches, expected returns and receipt scans. The marketplaces table is the root of per-account data scope. schema-import.sql adds lookup activation (staging, active, superseded), scan lines and issues, ticket history and the audit log, and schema-register.sql adds logistics partners, tracking evidence and persistent sessions. server/db.ts, the most depended-upon module in the graph, resolves DATABASE_URL with verified TLS and applies these additive, idempotent schema files in one guarded transaction at startup.
tour.languageLesson: SQL: an idempotent, additive migration usually uses CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS or ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, so the same file can run on every startup without harm. With a rule that tables and columns are never dropped, older rows stay readable while new columns are added beside them.

tour.title: Express API Bootstrap
tour.description: server/index.ts is the API's entry point and the root of its dependency tree. It configures Sentry, security and rate limiting, mounts every feature route module (register, uploads, claims, Iron Send, OMSGuru, Shopify, payments), serves the built web client, attaches the live WebSocket, initializes the database from Step 3 and starts the background schedulers. Route modules stay thin because of server/http.ts, which reads the user, account scope and actor that requireUser attached, enforces Admin or Supervisor access, and maps a ServiceError to its HTTP status. rate-limit.ts adds a sliding-window limiter with lockouts to protect sign-in against brute-force attempts.
tour.languageLesson: Express handles each request through a chain of middleware: every function gets (req, res, next) and either sends a response or calls next(). Because one middleware (requireUser here) attaches the user and scope to the request, later handlers can read them without repeating the authentication code.

tour.title: Sessions and Account Scope
tour.description: Before it returns any data, the server answers two questions: who is calling, and which marketplace accounts may they see? auth.ts issues persistent device sessions. Tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes, read from a cookie or a Bearer header, and subject to absolute and idle timeouts and revocation. access.ts has 44 incoming dependencies and holds the pure account-scope rules and SQL condition builders that every data route uses to bind the user's account list as a query parameter, which is the project's first rule. The users table stores the role and the all-marketplaces access flag these rules read.

tour.title: Loading Marketplace Lookup Data
tour.description: A scan is only useful if the server already knows which return to expect, so the first workflow is uploading a marketplace return report. sheets.ts parses CSV/XLSX grids, finds headers by name and maps Myntra, Flipkart, Meesho, Ajio and Amazon rows into ParsedRow records under strict identifier rules, using the pure normalizers in marketplace-rules.ts (return-type mapping, AWB repair, carrier detection). upload-routes.ts previews a file and stages it in memory, and upload-policy.ts lists the blockers and the confirmations the user must give. lookup-import.ts then commits the batch in one transaction, so it supersedes the account's active lookup rows while keeping the superseded rows.

tour.title: The Return Scan Register
tour.description: The return scan register is the core of the project: the permanent record of what physically arrived. register-rules.ts holds pure rules that never touch the database: tracking and ticket normalization, scan validation, lookup decisions, status derivation and row mapping. register-service.ts wraps those rules in transactions: account-scoped AWB lookup against the lookup rows from Step 6, idempotent scan recording under AWB advisory locks, issue correction and tickets. register-routes.ts exposes all of this over HTTP, bound to the caller's scope from Step 5, and docs/REGISTER.md specifies the 19 register columns and the rules for activation, concurrency and idempotency.
tour.languageLesson: Splitting a feature into a pure rules module and a transactional service follows the 'functional core, imperative shell' design. The rules can be unit-tested with plain inputs and outputs and no database, while the service owns I/O, locking and transactions. PostgreSQL advisory locks make two concurrent requests for the same AWB take turns on a key the application chooses, instead of locking whole tables.

tour.title: React Web Console
tour.description: Staff use the register through the React 19 web console in src/. App.tsx checks the cookie session through /api/auth/me, shows boot, error and login screens, picks the page from the URL path using routes.ts (scanners default to /scan), and provides the workspace context defined in workspace.tsx to every page. api.ts is a small fetch wrapper that sends HttpOnly cookie credentials and throws a typed ApiError. types.ts mirrors the server's records (scans, register rows, uploads, claims, Iron Send batches), so the client stays in step with the API from Steps 4 to 7.
tour.languageLesson: React context (createContext plus a Provider) gives every nested component values such as the signed-in user without passing props through each level. Wrapping it in a custom hook that throws when used outside the provider, as useWorkspace does, replaces a silent undefined with an immediate, clear error.

tour.title: Scanning and Live Sync
tour.description: ScanReturns.tsx is the browser's warehouse scan bench. It offers an AWB lookup that asks which account when more than one matches, per-item physical checks, issue capture (categories, tickets, Iron Send), client-side validation that mirrors the server rules from Step 7, and audio chimes. To keep every open screen current, server/live.ts authenticates /api/live WebSocket upgrades and pushes notifications of committed changes, filtered by account scope. src/live.tsx keeps one socket per tab, reconnects with exponential backoff, falls back to polling every 3.5 seconds, and exposes this through the useSyncState and useLiveChanges hooks.
tour.languageLesson: A custom React hook (a function whose name starts with use) packages stateful logic, such as a WebSocket subscription, so any component can reuse it. Keeping a single socket at module level and debouncing change events, as live.tsx does, avoids one connection per component and stops a burst of updates from re-rendering a page many times.

tour.title: Android Scanner App
tour.description: Most scanning happens on warehouse phones running the native Kotlin app in android/, which calls the same API. ReturnScanApp sets up the app-wide singletons (SessionManager, ApiClient, SoundManager, ImageCache) at startup. ScannerActivity and its activity_scanner.xml layout run continuous CameraX + ML Kit barcode scanning, AWB lookup, a verification sheet and audio and haptic verdict cues. AppUpdater checks the server's release manifest, downloads the APK, verifies its SHA-256 and opens the installer, and server/mobile-release.ts serves that manifest from GitHub releases with a bundled fallback, which is why every scanning change must ship with a matching release entry.
tour.languageLesson: Kotlin/Android: a subclass of Application is a single object that lives as long as the process, so it is a natural home for shared singletons such as an API client. Activities are recreated on events like screen rotation, so long-lived state belongs elsewhere. WorkManager schedules deferrable background work, such as the periodic update check, so that work survives app restarts.

tour.title: Claims and the Automation Queue
tour.description: When a scanned return arrives damaged or wrong, the business files a claim with the marketplace. claims-service.ts manages claim records, templates and Firebase-backed evidence tied to a scanned return. claim-automation-service.ts turns a claim into a queued job: it encrypts supplier credentials with AES-256-GCM, registers and authenticates automation agents, leases jobs under lease and authorization checks, and syncs tickets back into the register. claim-automation-routes.ts exposes the agent API (registration, heartbeat, job polling, progress, completion), claim-follow-up-service.ts schedules re-checks until a ticket is approved, rejected, paid or reconciled, and schema-claim-automation.sql adds the tables for credentials, agents, jobs and follow-ups.

tour.title: The Automation Engine
tour.description: The automation engine in desktop-agent/ is the agent that works through the queue from Step 11. desktop-app-server.ts owns the only claim-filing loop and the only ticket follow-up loop and serves its own HTTP API behind CORS and bearer-token checks. It uses agent-client.ts to register, send heartbeats, lease jobs and follow-ups, and stream evidence to disk. Both loops drive the same supplier browser profile, so poll-guard.ts keeps them from running at the same time, cycle-watchdog.ts races each cycle against a hard timeout so a hung network call cannot silence the bot, and engine-config.ts refuses to bind to a reachable address without an ENGINE_TOKEN of at least 24 characters.

tour.title: Marketplace Panel Automations
tour.description: Each supplier panel has its own automation class. registry.ts maps a marketplace name to its class (Meesho, Flipkart, Amazon, Myntra, Ajio), and base-automation.ts defines the abstract BaseMarketplaceAutomation contract, the result types for filing claims and checking tickets, and helpers for human-like typing, clicking and file uploads. meesho.ts is the fully automatic implementation: it submits the Raise a Ticket form and classifies each ticket page for follow-ups, while the other panels are assisted and answer 'not implemented' for ticket tracking. browser-runner.ts drives a system Chrome or Edge over CDP with a profile per panel and kills the whole process tree on close, and submit-guard.ts re-checks a freshly fetched job just before Submit so a stale or already-resolved claim is never filed.
tour.languageLesson: A TypeScript abstract class declares methods that subclasses must implement and shares concrete helpers with all of them. When a registry (a factory) picks the subclass by name, the engine calls one interface (file a claim, check a ticket) and each marketplace supplies its own portal steps. This combines the template-method and factory patterns.

tour.title: Desktop Shell and Renderer
tour.description: Operators watch and steer the engine through the Windows Electron app. desktop/main.ts applies switches for low-spec hardware, serves the bundled React renderer over the privileged returnapp://desktop scheme, starts or connects to the engine from Step 12, and hosts the supplier browser views. preload.cjs exposes a narrow window.desktopApp bridge through contextBridge: no raw ipcRenderer, no secrets, and every subscription returns an unsubscribe function. The renderer's App.tsx, engineApi.ts and Dashboard.tsx call the engine API without an Authorization header, because the shell adds the token, and show the 'All panels green' or 'Action required' headline, job KPIs and a live log.
tour.languageLesson: In Electron, contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld publishes a small, explicit API from the preload script into an isolated renderer. The web page can then request privileged actions over IPC without ever having Node or ipcRenderer access. Returning an unsubscribe function from every event subscription prevents duplicate listeners after the renderer reloads.

tour.title: Build, CI and Deployment
tour.description: The tour ends with the delivery pipeline. The root Dockerfile is a two-stage node:22-alpine build: the builder runs npm ci, the typecheck and the Vite + esbuild build, and the runner keeps only production dependencies and serves the API and web client on port 3001 as a non-root user. docker-compose.production.yml runs that image on the Hostinger VPS behind Traefik with Let's Encrypt TLS. ci.yml runs the typecheck, the build and the full test suite against a throwaway postgres:16 database on every push and pull request. desktop-release.yml fails a desktop PR that does not bump the version and publishes the NSIS installer as a desktop-v release, and deploy/engine/Dockerfile packages the engine from Step 12 for headless Linux with Chromium and a 256 MB heap.
tour.languageLesson: A multi-stage Docker build uses several FROM stages: the builder stage has dev dependencies and compilers, and the final stage copies in only the built output and production dependencies, so the image is smaller and has less attack surface. Copying package files and running npm ci before copying the source lets Docker reuse the cached dependency layer when only the code changes.
